newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
BBC CHIEFS PUT CURB ON TV SEX

Sir Christopher Bland Chairman of the BBC, today announced a tough new code of practice for TV producers. The "comprehensive code of ethics for broadcasting' demands that before the 9pm watershed swearing, explicit sex and violence will not be tolerated.

A report by the Institute of Chartered Accountants claims that an exponential rise in its membership will lead to too many accountants competing for too few jobs, and many being forced to take large wage cuts.
BUBA PAVES THE WAY FOR SOARING DOLLAR
Comments by Hans Tietmeyer, president of the Bundesbank, that he wanted a weaker mark, caused a big rise to over 1.50 against the Deutschmark overnight.
PPP TO BUY LONDON HOSPITALS STAKE

PPP, the private healthcare group, is to make its first step into the private hospitals market, following its purchase of a 50 percent stake alongside Columbia/HCA, the largest private healthcare provider in the world, in a joint venture to run four top private hospitals in London.
ROTHSCHILD IN RECORD FORM WITH MERGERS

Amid a record year for mergers in Europe and the US, the now global merchant banking house of Rothschild is set for its best year ever. Rothschild in London, New York and Paris has advised on some of the biggest utiities and telecoms takeovers this year. BT's takeover of MCI will generate an estimated $25 million for Rothschild, which will stop current speculation that it needs to merge with a large investment banking company to survive.
HAWK DEAL PUTS BAe ON COURSE FOR BIGGER TARGET

As a result of this week's 1 billion stg order for the Hawk fighter trainer, British Aerospace's Australian subsidiary has far achieved its chief Robin Southwell's aim for an increase in its annual turnover. Less than a year later the company's turnover has come from a modest 100mn Australian dollars to 250 million Australian dollars.
